VERDICT: CLEAN

BOUNDARY: The proof deals with a concrete nondegenerate interval [0,1] with a<b, a bounded function, and no empty/family or choice branches. The endpoint cases are handled implicitly because the open subintervals (t_i, t_{i+1}) are guaranteed nonempty and the Darboux sums are well‑defined. The usual degenerate cases (a=b, empty domain) are excluded by hypothesis. No hidden division, limit swap, or index shift is involved.

SOURCES: Every cited item in the target’s dependency list—fs-bounded-implies-riemann-integrable, def-dirichlet-and-thomae-functions, def-darboux-sums, def-darboux-integral, def-partition-and-refinement, lem-q-and-irrationals-dense-r, thm-closure-characterisations-r, def-interior-closure-boundary-r, def-neighbourhood-r, lem-finite-sum-laws, def-finite-sum, def-bounded-set, def-interval, def-infimum, def-max-min, def-complete-ordered-field, def-ordered-field, lem-of-add-order, lem-of-sign-rules—was inspected in its supplied full text. Each supplies exactly the property invoked: density gives a rational and an irrational in every nonempty open interval; partition definitions give strictly positive subinterval lengths summing to 1; Darboux definitions give the lower and upper integrals as sup/inf of the respective sums; singletons have themselves as sup and inf; finite‑sum laws justify zero and constant sums; ordered‑field axioms give 0≠1.

CHECKED: Title, public claim (“The Dirichlet function … is bounded and not Riemann integrable”), all numbered proof steps (1.1, 1.2, 2.1, 3.1, 4.1), and Remarks were reviewed. The argument correctly exhibits g bounded, forces every lower Darboux sum to 0 and every upper sum to 1, obtains lower integral 0 and upper integral 1, and concludes non‑integrability, thereby refuting the false statement. No logical gap, missing hypothesis, or counterexample was found.
